messages:
sara (support): FYI customer reported what looks like overbilling on their Dedicated pool. They say invoice INV-2026-042 shows 200 reserved GPU hours billed but the dashboard & metering CSV show ~60 GPU-hours consumed. Ticket 9876 attached. Can someone take a look?

kevin (CS): Thanks — can you paste the invoice line and pool id? timeframe? Any indication of burst usage?

sara (support): Pool dp-42, tenant acme-corp. Time window 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-15. Customer said they used burst for a short test on 3/10 but otherwise steady low usage. Invoice line: "INV-2026-042 | reserved_capacity_hours | 200". They also have an SLA credit line on the invoice which is odd as they expected a debit.

maria (billing): Pulling invoice. I see the 200 reserved hours line. On metering side I can see entries aggregated to ~62 hours for dp-42 in that window. Two quick possibilities: (1) reserved hours applied at billing cycle boundary incorrectly, (2) burst router or fallback assigned compute to reserved pool but token attribution landed elsewhere.

nathan (infra): Can you export the metering rows for dp-42? run: 
```
redwood-cli metering export --tenant acme-corp --from 2026-03-01 --to 2026-03-15 --pool dp-42 --format csv
```
Paste a snippet here.

sara (support): Pasting redacted snippet below (cols: ts,pool,consumed_hours,tokens,billing_tag):
```
2026-03-03T02:11:00Z,dp-42,0.25,512,reserved
2026-03-10T12:05:11Z,dp-42,5.00,450000,burst
2026-03-12T07:40:09Z,dp-42,0.00,0,reserved
2026-03-12T07:40:10Z,dp-42,120.00,0,reserved
```

kevin (CS): That 120h single row on 3/12 looks suspicious — 0 tokens but huge billed hours. Likely a metering aggregation or retry duplicate. Do we have the raw metering job logs around that time?

billing-bot: Metering job finished: 2026-03-12T07:41:02Z, job_id=mtr-20260312-071. Processed 4,321 records.

maria (billing): If metering erroneously recorded a long-running allocation with 0 tokens (possible a stuck allocation record), billing would charge reserved hours while token counters remain low. Need to reconcile raw allocation events with token streams.

nathan (infra): I'm going to check router/allocator logs for dp-42 for that window. Quick grep command: 
```
curl -s "https://logs.internal/redwood/router?pool=dp-42&from=2026-03-12T00:00&to=2026-03-13T00:00" | jq '.[] | select(.event=="alloc_start" or .event=="alloc_end")'
```

sara (support): Running the reconcile helper now: 
```
python tools/reconcile_reserved_hours.py --invoice INV-2026-042 --pool dp-42 --from 2026-03-01 --to 2026-03-15
```
Result: "billed_reserved_hours=198.5, metered_consumed_hours=62.1, unmatched_reserved_hours=136.4"

kevin (CS): That delta is too big to be a rounding issue. Nathan, any evidence of an allocator stuck/ghost allocation on 3/12?

nathan (infra): Found allocator trace: alloc_id=alloc-9f3, pool=dp-42, start=2026-03-12T07:40:09Z, end=2026-03-12T07:40:10Z, but metering job ingested it as 120h due to a bad duration multiplier when an upstream heartbeat was missing. Repro: when heartbeat missing, duration gets multiplied by retention_factor (bug INF-2307).

maria (billing): Okay — that's a clear root cause. We should correct the invoice for INV-2026-042 (remove the ~136.4 hours) and issue a credit. I'll open an adjustment PR but need finance approval for customer credit.

kevin (CS): Agreed. For transparency, let's offer the customer a provisional credit and an RCA once fixed. Sara can you confirm the email text and credit amount?

sara (support): Draft to customer: "Hi — we found a metering bug that caused a spurious 120h allocation to be counted toward your reserved pool on 2026-03-12. We're issuing a credit for the incorrectly billed hours and will update your invoice INV-2026-042. Internal ticket INF-2307 tracks the fix. Apologies for the noise. — Sara". Proposed credit = 136.4 * rate_per_hour (TBD by finance).

maria (billing): I'll calculate numeric credit and include SLA credits already applied. Provisional credit: $8,184 (will confirm). cc @finance.

nathan (infra): Patch for INF-2307 is queued: fix heartbeats -> duration calc. Deploy to metering staging now, then run reprocess for affected jobs.

kevin (CS): Next actions: 1) maria to compute and apply invoice adjustment 2) nathan to reprocess metering & close INF-2307 3) sara to send customer note and set expectation for RCA. Any objections?

sara (support): No objections. I'll send the note after maria confirms dollar amount. :thumbsup:

maria (billing): Confirmed final credit amount $8,200 (rounded). Applied as invoice adjustment and created credit memo CM-2026-198. Notifying customer now.

kevin (CS): Thanks team. Once reprocess completes, reconcile and close ticket 9876. :white_check_mark:
